lessons.title: The ticket-office ledger
lessons.status: 16 new narrated and illustrated scenes across the pair; awaiting recording, encoding, device playback and public release

canonical_slot.bridge: Watch what changes when a plain ticket becomes a star ticket. Later, use the same idea to count only the extra seats in each matched pair.

revisits.bridge: Match each two-seat ticket with one four-seat ticket. Compared with giving every ticket one seat, how many extra seats does that same pair explain each time?
The ledger fixes both the number of tickets and the number of seats. Which third clue lets you connect the numbers of two-seat and four-seat tickets before solving for singles?

lessons.title: The domino seam workshop
lessons.status: 16 new narrated and illustrated scenes across the pair; awaiting recording, encoding, device playback and public release

canonical_slot.bridge: Trace the seam between columns three and four. If just one domino crossed it, how many cells would still need covering on the left?

revisits.bridge: In the film, count the cells left on one side of the seam after a single crossing. In your lesson, count cells by colour and ask how many of each colour a tile covers.
The glued domino in column two divides the board. Which parts can you now tile independently? Compare that split with the two rooms left when both seam crossings are forced.

canonical_slot.bridge: Follow the three pairs into the ledger. When you subtract a pair from the total of all three boxes, which box stays behind?

revisits.bridge: Add the two stationery receipts. How many sets of one notebook and one ruler are in the combined purchase? Find the price of that set before finding either item separately.
In the three-box ledger, count how many times each box appears across the three pairs. Why can you halve the sum before subtracting the pair that omits one box?

canonical_slot.bridge: At the left edge, put a horizontal domino in the top row. Which cell now forces a second horizontal domino underneath?

revisits.bridge: Compare the board with two corners missing and the two-row domino strip. The area test rules out one tiling. Which boundary cell determines the next move on the other board?
When the first two horizontal dominoes form a block, cover that block with your hand. What smaller board remains, and how would fixing a middle piece divide it into two parts?
